data.name: Merry
data.gender_notes: Merry is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘myrige’, meaning ‘wondrous, merry’. The name was popularized by the character in Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol. The name Merry carries the meaning “Joyful, Cheerful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Merry usually hope their child will grow to embody joyful, cheerful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to bring joy and happiness to others.
data.etymology: Merry belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joyful, Cheerful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Merry total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Merry" gained popularity during the Victorian era, and its association with the celebration of Christmas has become deeply ingrained in Western culture. It embodies a sense of joy, merriment, and cheer which is often invoked during this festive season.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Merry" can also be seen as a reflection of the spiritual essence of the Christmas season - a time of wonder, joy, and celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ. It serves as a reminder to approach life with a light-hearted, joyful spirit, even in the midst of adversity. The name can be seen as a call to embrace the beauty and wonder of life and approach each day with a sense of joy and purpose.
